column1: # What b37e6ae0 -- the parent of the Stage 2 lane that grounded lambda-shape evidence on the FABRIC native reference --
# decided and said for every guest mixin of LambdaShapeEvidenceStagedTest's merged-base corpus, read by
# Columns: pruner arm (off/on) <TAB> guest mixin <TAB> inputs <TAB> decisions.
#   inputs     LambdaShapeEvidenceStagedTest.inputs: the guest's class file, each target as KernelBoot's pre-Mixin chain
#              handed it to Mixin under that arm, and the pruner's record for those targets (16 hex of a SHA-256).
#   decisions  LambdaShapeEvidenceStagedTest.Decisions.digest over what decide() collects: MixinHandlerShim's landing and
#              wraps, InsertedLambdaArgumentShim's moves, MixinFit's verdict, and MixinOverloadPin's and MixinFit's words.
# Recorded 2026-10-30 on the staged root 26.2.0.93 (merged base + both carriers) and the local packs: 161 guests, both
# arms. The inputs were dumped by the staged test committed with this table; at b37e6ae0 a test holding a verbatim copy of
# decide(), signature() and Decisions.digest read them back (NativeGameReferences bound over the same three jars, the
# pruner's record replayed through recordDroppedForTest; lambda-decisions-generator.java.txt) and wrote these rows; every
# one matched the new code with the reference off and on. A row is keyed by its inputs, so a rebuilt base or a changed chain transformer leaves rows this
# machine no longer reproduces: they are counted, not judged. Keep decide()'s strings as they are, or nothing compares.
